overall_summary: Deduplication of 94 rows yields 47 unique videos. Performance is heavily stratified: visceral first-person 'What If You Fell Into...' cosmic survival scenarios and extreme exoplanet environments dominate both aggregate views (800–1,050+ views) and engagement (likes-per-view up to 3.7%). Conversely, repetitive psychology trivia ('fake memories', 'songs stuck in head') and recycling identical titles show catastrophic drop-off down to single-digit views. Optimal duration is tightly clustered around 19–21 seconds.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Sensory 'What If You Fell Into...' Planetary Survival Hook
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (824 views, 15 likes) represent the channel's top tier.
winning_patterns.action: Center upcoming content on first-person visceral survival scenarios navigating mind-bending alien environments with step-by-step physical consequences.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) drove over 5x the channel average view count.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight extreme, paradox-driven planetary physics using comparative superlatives.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' scraped 5 to 10 views; 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' produced only 17 views.
weak_patterns.action: Discontinue abstract, low-stakes cognitive trivia shorts; reallocate production capacity toward high-stakes cosmic what-if and survival storytelling.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeatedly publishing identical titles ('Why Space Is Completely Silent', 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts', 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') led to severe view erosion (collapsing from 220 to 34 views).
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict uniqueness constraints: never reuse identical premises or title formulas across rolling 30-day windows.

next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that Titan's atmosphere is so thick and gravity so light that strapped-on wings would let a human fly like a bird, but falling in means freezing into solid glass in under two seconds.
next_video.reason: Leverages the channel's single highest-converting hook mechanic ('What If You Fell Into...') while introducing a fresh celestial entity (Saturn's moon Titan / Kraken Mare) never before featured on FACTVERSE.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not cover TrES-2b, 55 Cancri e, Gliese 436b, HD 189733b, or generic diamond/ice/ruby planets already published.
Keep duration strictly between 19 and 21 seconds to match high-retention winners.
